primitives.does: Resolve the intended recipient and the route permitted for a document of this type. A document reaching the wrong party is worse than one not sent - the second can be retried and the first cannot be recalled

Bind the distribution to the exact issued version. Sending an outdated version is the failure this step exists to prevent: the recipient then holds, relies on, and may sign terms that nobody currently offers

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it

primitives.purpose: Raise the actual delivery through the canonical communication mechanism, which owns channels, permissions, retries and delivery evidence.
primitives.brief: Raise the actual delivery through the canonical communication mechanism, which owns channels, permissions, retries and delivery evidence. Document distribution does not build its own delivery path - a parallel one will disagree with the canonical delivery record about whether the contract was ever sent
primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

cancelOn.meaning: distribution is confirmed to the required level

primitives.reads: the the issued version re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

branches.label: Failed

primitives.does: Record DELIVERED or AVAILABLE against the exact version distributed. Delivery state describes the distribution and never the document - an undelivered contract is a valid contract nobody has, and treating delivery as validity turns a mail failure into a legal one

primitives.state: the identified version reached the intended recipient; the document's validity is unchanged by this
primitives.reEntry: a superseding version requires its own distribution. Nothing about this one is retracted by that - the recipient was correctly given what was current then

primitives.does: Record the distribution outcome as unknown and do not treat it as delivered. The document's validity is untouched either way - what is unknown is whether anybody has it

primitives.on: a distribution whose outcome could not be established
carries: the version, the recipient and everything last known about the delivery
the explicit fact that the document remains valid and issued regardless of how this resolves
the failure as the channel reported it, and the exact version that was being sent
the explicit requirement that any fallback route carries the same version - a recovery that sends a different one is worse than the original failure
